standard_prerequisites.name: Cut (Dedekind cut)
standard_prerequisites.statement: A cut is a non-empty proper subset of the rationals that is downward closed under the order and has no greatest element.
standard_prerequisites.use: The first half of the proof verifies the three clauses of this definition for the union lambda (source lines 952-965).

standard_prerequisites.name: Upper bound of a set of cuts
standard_prerequisites.statement: A cut beta is an upper bound of a set S of cuts when every member of S is contained in beta.
standard_prerequisites.use: The hypothesis that S has an upper bound is used twice: to obtain a rational outside lambda (source lines 956-958) and, in the form of a general beta, to show that lambda is the least upper bound (source lines 966-967).

core_obligations: Form the union lambda of S and verify it is a cut: use the upper bound to see that at least one cut is in S and that some rational is absent from every member of S (so lambda is non-empty and proper), then use downward closure of the individual cuts for the second clause, and the absence of a greatest element in each cut for the third (source lines 949-965).
Show that lambda is an upper bound of S: every member of S is contained in its union, so each member is a subset of lambda (source lines 966-967).

Show that lambda is the least upper bound: given another upper bound beta, take any rational p in lambda, choose a member of S containing p, and use that beta contains that member to conclude p is in beta; generalise to lambda contained in beta (source lines 967).

proof_roadmap.step: Form the union lambda of the given non-empty set S of cuts.
Verify the three clauses of the definition of a cut for lambda.
Show lambda is an upper bound and, by an element-wise argument, the least one.

difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the author's own theorem realcompleteness at source lines 944-946: the set of cuts, ordered by inclusion, has the least-upper-bound property. The proof at source lines 948-968 is the classical Dedekind construction and is not a routine application of a stated completeness axiom in the unit. It starts from an arbitrary non-empty set S of cuts with an upper bound, forms the union lambda, and then has to verify the three clauses of the definition of a cut one by one: that lambda is non-empty and strictly smaller than the rationals (which uses both hypotheses, and where the strictness needs the upper bound to supply a rational absent from every member of S), that lambda is downward closed under the order on rationals, and that lambda has no greatest element. Only after that does it prove the two upper-bound clauses, first that lambda contains every member of S, then that any other upper bound contains lambda, again by an element-wise argument. The order in which the hypotheses are used is not visible in the statement. No result outside the retained text is used.
